title: Rotate Non Negative Elements
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, rotate only the non-negative elements to the left by k positions.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, rotate only the non-negative elements to the left by k positions. Negative elements remain unchanged. Place the rotated non-negative elements back into their original non-negative positions, skipping negatives. Return the modified array.
constraints: nums has up to 100,000 signed integers and k is nonnegative.
Negative values and their positions never change.
Cyclically rotate only the nonnegative subsequence left by k positions.
reference_solution:
def rotate_nonnegative_elements(nums,k):
    values=[value for value in nums if value>=0]
    if not values:return nums[:]
    shift=k%len(values);rotated=values[shift:]+values[:shift];answer=nums[:];position=0
    for index,value in enumerate(nums):
        if value>=0:answer[index]=rotated[position];position+=1
    return answer

hints: Negative positions form fixed holes; only the ordered nonnegative subsequence changes.
Extract that subsequence, reduce k modulo its length, and concatenate suffix then prefix for a left rotation.
Write the rotated values back into exactly the original nonnegative positions.
Extraction and reinsertion preserve every negative slot, while cyclic indexing produces precisely k left moves.
editorial: Extraction and reinsertion preserve every negative slot, while cyclic indexing produces precisely k left moves.

tests.explanation: The nonnegative sequence [1,3] rotates left by one to [3,1].
Rotating [5,4,6] left by two gives [6,5,4] in the same nonnegative slots.
